definition.text: The state an industry reaches when firms can enter or leave it almost freely, so that competition pushes each firm's economic profit to zero.

facts.text: If firms earn positive economic profit, newcomers join until it is gone; if they make losses, firms leave until profit rises back to zero.
The zero-profit situation is called the industry's long run and is close to perfect competition.
In gold rushes few prospectors got rich, but many people built successful businesses selling shovels.
In neoclassical models, a market economy of profit-seeking firms is compatible with zero growth because of this condition.
